## Natural history notes

A medium-sized kissing bug characterized by a flattened dark brown to black body, cone-shaped head, long slender legs, and orange to reddish markings along the edges of the abdomen. In Florida, the Eastern Bloodsucking Conenose occurs in wooded areas, hammocks, pine flatwoods, yards, animal shelters, and places where it can find vertebrate hosts such as mammals, birds, or reptiles. It feeds on blood at night and can bite people or pets; because triatomine bugs can transmit the parasite that causes Chagas disease through infected feces rather than the bite itself, it should not be handled and any indoor specimens should be collected carefully for identification.
